stem.en: A farmer's banana plants are infected by a virus. He wants healthy plants of the same variety in large numbers. What should he use?

text.en: Healthy plantlets raised from shoot tips

feedback.en: Yes. Tissue culture gives many healthy plantlets of one variety.

text.en: Stem pieces taken from his infected plants

feedback.en: Pieces of infected plants can carry the virus into the new crop.

text.en: Grafts from his infected banana plants

feedback.en: A graft of an infected plant can carry the infection with it.

text.en: Soil brought in from a neighbour's field

feedback.en: New soil does not give him new plants, and the plants carry the virus.

explanation.en: Tissue culture uses the shoot tip to make many healthy plantlets of one variety. This helps farmers eliminate virus-infected plants and get high yields.

hints.en: Which choice gives many plants of the same variety?
Which choice avoids using parts of infected plants?
